title: codegen-quant-kernel-overhead-compiler-pass-profiles-apr2025
content:
TL;DR:
We found that differences in compiler/codegen passes (memplan, fusion, vectorize) produce measurable overheads in quantized kernels beyond algorithmic compute savings. In one bad codegen config INT8 AWQ kernels experienced ~18% lower net token throughput vs an equivalent codegen with tiling+fusion enabled due to extra memcpy and suboptimal kernel shapes.

Purpose:
Quick field experiment to understand why some quantized kernels (AWQ/GPTQ) underperform on our fleet even when theoretical FLOPs are lower. Hypothesis: the compiler/pass ordering used for kernel generation (and autoscheduler heuristics) can introduce memory copies, misaligned vector widths, and small-kernel fragmentation that dominates runtime for short sequences.

Experiment setup (synthetic + replay):
- HW: A100 80GB (p5), H100-80GB (p6) for parity checks.
- Models: Llama-2-13B (FP16 baseline), AWQ-int8 variant, GPTQ-int4 baseline (for reference).
- Sequences: synthetic short (prompt+50 tokens), mixed (prompt+250 tokens), long (prompt+2048 tokens) to stress different kernel shapes.
- Workload: single-request latency and steady-state throughput (100 concurrent clients synthetic harness).
- Codegen pass variants tested:
  * baseline-codegen (current prod: memplan=v2, fusion=off, vectorize=auto)
  * fused-tiling-codegen (memplan=v3, fusion=on, tile-size=128, vectorize=on)
  * conservative-codegen (memplan=v1, fusion=off, vectorize=off)
- Kernel flavors: small-block (64x64), medium (128x64), packed(256x64) generated by codegen.
- Instrumentation: CUPTI traces for kernel times, host->device memcpy timings, nvprof to confirm occupancy, our in-process tracer to attribute time to "kernel_compute" vs "memcpy" vs "dispatch_overhead".

Raw (representative) numbers — short sequence (prompt+50), median over 500 runs on A100:
- FP16 baseline (fused-tiling-codegen): 320 tokens/s, kernel_compute 60ms, memcpy 4.3ms, dispatch 1.0ms
- AWQ INT8 (fused-tiling-codegen): 590 tokens/s, kernel_compute 32ms, memcpy 3.8ms, dispatch 0.9ms
- AWQ INT8 (baseline-codegen): 486 tokens/s, kernel_compute 34ms, memcpy 18.7ms, dispatch 1.5ms
- GPTQ INT4 (conservative-codegen): 720 tokens/s, kernel_compute 28ms, memcpy 26.2ms, dispatch 2.0ms

Key observation 1 — memcpy / shape chopping dominates:
- The baseline-codegen emitted many small kernels (tile sizes ~64) with buffer allocations per tile; host-side and device-side memcpy overhead increased sharply. Even though kernel_compute saved cycles, the memcpy overhead reduced end-to-end benefit. The fused-tiling-codegen avoided this by emitting larger tiled kernels with in-kernel shared-memory staging.

Key observation 2 — vector alignment matters for AWQ kernels:
- When vectorize=off, we saw a ~9% perf regression for AWQ kernels because quant packing produced misaligned lanes. Enabling vectorize collapsed small memory ops into aligned wide loads and improved throughput.

Key observation 3 — compiler heuristics and occupancy:
- The autoscheduler chose a kernel shape that looked optimal by FLOP model but produced registers spills at runtime on the A100 variant, leading to reduced occupancy and unexpected L2 thrash. This was visible in nvprof as lower SM active cycles despite similar kernel_compute times reported by the driver.

Quality tradeoffs (very coarse):
- AWQ (int8): BLEU/QA accuracy drop vs FP16: ~0.6–1.2 absolute points depending on eval set; subjective fuzziness increased on long-context retrieval prompts. But cost/throughput gains make AWQ still compelling if net throughput is realized.
- GPTQ (int4): smaller quality hit in our eval but more fragile to sequence length and sensitive to codegen shape fragmentation.

Actionable fixes tried during experiment:
1) Force fused-tiling-codegen for quantized model builds — instant ~18% throughput uplift for AWQ vs baseline-codegen on short sequences.
2) Add a post-codegen pass to detect tiny kernel emits (< 8KB per tile) and fuse them into batch kernels where possible.
3) Add a vector alignment sanity check after quant packing to re-pad weights to 32-byte lanes when beneficial.
4) For autoscheduler: add a runtime-feedback loop that penalizes kernels producing >2 memcpys per sequence.

Tradeoffs and caveats:
- Fusing tiles increases peak device RAM transient usage; on memory-constrained instances this can push us into OOM for very long sequences. Need guardrails per-instance-type.
- Some customer corpora (sparse long prompts) benefit from small kernels — a blanket fuse-policy would regress those. Need traffic-aware policy.

Open questions / TODOs:
- (A) Re-run same experiment on H100 and inference-optimized instances (p7) — codegen-memory behavior may differ because H100 has different L2 and vector width.
- (B) Integrate automated detection into our build pipeline: a build-time codegen validator that runs a short synthetic harness and rejects codegen configs that cause >10% memcpy cost.
- (C) Evaluate whether specialized memcpy-elision helpers (cudaMemcpyAsync with pinned staging buffer + host coalescing) reduce the penalty without fusing kernels.
- (D) Measure impact on cold-start/warmup (we saw small warmup penalty when fused kernels increase JIT compile time).

Notes-to-self / rough checklist:
- Add flamegraph snippets to the doc — export from nvprof and inline (TODO).
- Create a small e2e reproduction harness with 3 random customer prompts (PR in linked_artifacts).
- Coordinate with infra to reserve 2x H100 machines for validation (Liam).

Suggested rollout plan (conservative):
1) Feature-flag fused-tiling-codegen for AWQ builds in canary region only.
2) Run 48h canary with traffic-weighted mix (short/mid/long). Monitor: 95p latency, memcpy fraction, OOMs, eval quality regression + rollout guard rails.
3) If stable, expand to 50% then full.

Appendix: quick microprofile snapshots (short sequence):
- baseline-codegen, AWQ-int8:
  * total_p99_latency: 94ms
  * device_kernel_time_avg: 34.2ms
  * total_memcpy_time_avg: 18.7ms (60% host->device staging, 40% device->device)
  * dispatch_overhead_avg: 1.5ms
- fused-tiling-codegen, AWQ-int8:
  * total_p99_latency: 58ms
  * device_kernel_time_avg: 32.1ms
  * total_memcpy_time_avg: 3.8ms
  * dispatch_overhead_avg: 0.9ms

Short takeaways for product/SEs:
- If customers see AWQ/AOT quantized models underperforming in short prompt patterns, the likely culprit is codegen fragmentation and memcpy overhead, not quant algorithm itself.
- Recommend turning on fused-tiling-codegen for cases where short latency matters; keep conservative-codegen as option for memory-constrained long-context workloads.
